question_en: What are the main mineral in the specimen shown, the original mineral whose crystal shape has been preserved, and the associated mineral? What is the specimen’s locality?
answer: Primary mineral: cuprian smithsonite; Original mineral: azurite; Associated mineral: mimetite; Locality: Tsumeb, Namibia
gold_trajectory:
# Detailed Simulated Search Trajectory · 2-2-E01

## Step 01 · Observe branching structure, establish query without presupposing mineral names

**Action:** First record the shape from the problem image, then search for records with specimen photos using "green drusy mineral branching crystal cast" or "green mineral pseudomorph branching". Green only helps narrow the image scope; it does not directly equal malachite, nor can it be used to determine chemical composition.

**Evidence Observation:** In the black background, there are tall and wide upright branches at the rear, narrow elongated branches at the lower left, and curved branches extending nearly horizontally to the right with upturned ends. The surface is covered with a light green fine-crystal crust; the middle curved branch and the white areas at the right end can serve as matching positions. The problem requires four items: primary mineral, original mineral, associated mineral, and locality, so a record of this specific specimen must be found.

## Step 02 · Locate SC-80 photo, align with problem image point by point

**Action:** Search for photos of the same shape in the Tsumeb pseudomorph specimen gallery, open the SC-80 section of the Sussman collection, and compare the associated John Schneider photo with the input.

**Evidence Observation:** The rear three-dimensional main branch layout, the upturned end of the right-extending curved branch, and the white crystal crust zones in the SC-80 photo all correspond to the input; the dimensions recorded on the page are 9 × 7 × 4 cm, which can be used to confirm the entry identity. Dimensions and collection history are only backend positioning information; the problem does not require outputting them.

Specimen gallery:
https://tsumebfineminerals.com/sussman12a.html

SC-80 original photo:
https://www.tsumebfineminerals.com/sussman/smithsonit20ps1.jpg

**Result of this step:** Bind the image to the specific SC-80 record to avoid answering based solely on a typical photo of one green mineral.

## Step 03 · Review similar pseudomorphs, distinguish same-species relationship from same-specimen identity

**Action:** Compare the four saved groups of similar photos, prioritizing branches, plate surfaces, and openings; do not use color depth as the main distinguishing factor.

- HALP-18 also belongs to smithsonite after azurite, featuring a large opening at the rear right, a wide plate at the front, and a tubular part extending to the left; these do not equal the three open main branches in the problem image. It is not a candidate for "incorrect mineral relationship" but is another specimen; its specific underground stratigraphic position cannot be borrowed.
- SC-53's rosasite after malachite after azurite shows relatively obvious flat plates and crystal face outlines; MS-147's smithsonite after tarnowitzite features dense multi-columnar structures, relatively square ends, and small protrusions at the base. Neither matches the sparse curved branch layout of the input.
- Harvard TSNB686's malachite after azurite has relatively wide, stacked horizontal plate surfaces; even if associated records also show mimetite/smithsonite, SC-80 cannot be replaced due to similar keywords.

HALP-18 entry and photo:
https://www.irocks.com/minerals/specimen/48227

https://www.irocks.com/storage/media/94120/conversions/halp018a-wm-large.jpg

SC-53 and MS-147 comparison photos:
https://www.tsumebfineminerals.com/sussman/rosasite%2053.jpg

https://www.tsumebfineminerals.com/sussman/smit4abg.jpg

Harvard TSNB686 entry and photo:
https://tmn.fas.harvard.edu/objects/TSNB686

https://tmn.fas.harvard.edu/_astro/Exhibit1.MGMH87502_Malachite_ps_Azurite_133mm_Southwood.BOaRQkzm_Z27N4cP.webp

## Step 04 · Extract four items from matching record and end search

**Action:** Re-read the title and description of SC-80, and split "Cuprian Smithsonite ps. after Azurite with Mimetite; Tsumeb, Namibia" into the four items required by the problem.

**Evidence Observation:** The primary mineral is cuprian smithsonite; the original mineral whose crystal shape has been preserved is azurite; the associated mineral is mimetite; the locality is Tsumeb, Namibia. The description regarding the crystal crust covering and preserving the original azurite form supports this sequential relationship. The tiny mimetite was not independently identified at the current photo scale but is explicitly recorded in the matched entry.

Harvard's Azurite background entry also lists that smithsonite can form azurite pseudomorphs, used to verify the plausibility of this relationship; it does not replace the specific identification of SC-80:
https://tmn.fas.harvard.edu/objects/TSNB38/

**Stopping condition:** Image correspondence and all four text records are complete; directly output the four answer items without expanding on collection history, chemical analysis, or more specimens of the same mineral species.

## Formal Answer

Primary mineral: cuprian smithsonite; Original mineral: azurite; Associated mineral: mimetite; Locality: Tsumeb, Namibia
